args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), error rate 18%. The v2.3.1-rc release had also been unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run it, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Because v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before, the rollback didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Incident:** The SEV2 incident for checkout-api is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It covers the failure, the rollback and the health check afterwards. It also notes that the release candidate for v2.3.1 was already unhealthy in staging, and that the root cause needs to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
